name: Four kinds of responsibility
idea: An encyclopedia entry says the work's author defined corporate social responsibility as a four-part framework of economic, legal, ethical and discretionary (philanthropic) elements that society has of organizations, as of a given point in time. It adds that another writer considered the author's description of it as a pyramid of economic, legal, ethical and philanthropic responsibilities.
suggests: Check which kind of responsibility each part of the company's plan serves, economic, legal, ethical or philanthropic, and which kinds the plan leaves out.
limits: The entry notes that corporate social responsibility has been defined in many ways with little agreement, in part because different interests are represented.
competing_idea: The entry reports a different view, held by one writer and others: a corporation exists to maximize shareholder returns, and obeying the law counts as socially responsible behavior.
questions: Which economic, legal, ethical and philanthropic responsibilities does the company face in this decision?
Which of these responsibilities does the plan meet, and which does it leave out?
Who would define the company's responsibility differently, and what interest lies behind that view?

originals.reference: "Corporate social responsibility", Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia, article as last edited on 7 November 2026
originals.about: Archie B. Carroll, "The pyramid of corporate social responsibility: Toward the moral management of organizational stakeholders", Business Horizons, Vol. 34 No. 4, July 1991, pp. 39-48
